verify.why:
I re-read eForms CAN 23646227 (00755894-2023, subtype 29), which is the tender's only version, and I could not refute the reader. The notice has no procedure-level money: no BT-161 total, no BT-709 framework maximum and no BT-27 estimate. Its money is BT-720 on each of 108 LotTenders plus BT-710/711 (lowest and highest tender) on each of 12 LotResults. The 29 SettledContracts carry no amounts. Each one points to tenders in several lots, for example CON-0007 Cronos covers all of lots 1-12. Each LotResult then references every whole contract that has a tender in that lot.

I checked the served per-lot awards against the notice. Each one equals exactly the sum, over the contracts that LotResult references, of each contract's tenders across ALL of its lots. So LOT-0001 serves EUR 511,159,951.40, while its own 9 tenders total EUR 64,939,785.43 (7.87x). LOT-0010 serves EUR 735,028,699.27 against EUR 213,272,412.74 of its own tenders (3.45x). Every lot is inflated by 3.45x to 8.72x.

Adding up each contract's value times the number of LotResults that reference it gives exactly EUR 6,133,889,213.02, the served sum. In that sum CON-0007 (EUR 110,339,020) is counted 12 times and CON-0001 3D-ICT (EUR 64,282,900) 7 times. The distinct money in the notice is EUR 1,044,585,717.59. That figure is the same whether you add all 108 tenders, add the 29 contracts once each, or add each lot's own tenders. The served sum is 5.87x that.

No total is stated in the notice and there is no estimate, so the 10x-estimate guard had nothing to compare against. The old head was one lot's award copy (at most EUR 735m, about 0.70x of the distinct total) or null. Either was closer than EUR 6.13bn. The summed lots are distinct lots, but their award figures overlap, so the sum counts the same contracts several times. It is also farther from the true total.

A caveat: even EUR 1.04bn is only the sum of multi-supplier framework bid prices, not a stated ceiling. That does not rescue the 6.13bn figure. Files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-tender-db/3050fd14-5ca6-5dd7-8b63-f827e13fd8ce/scratchpad/v551/t1160515/ (detail.json, content.xml).

verify.why:
I could not refute the reader. I re-read CAN 47377529 (eForms subtype 29) and CN 25850497 myself.

- **The CN gives no estimate.** It has no money fields at all. It describes a French "accord-cadre multi-attributaires a marches subsequents" for gas, with 2 lots, at most 10 holders per lot (BT-113 = 10), 48 months.
- **The CAN's lot figures.**
  - LOT-0001: BT-709 framework maximum is 97,514,000 EUR. The 4 supplier tenders (ENGIE, TotalEnergies, Gaz de Bordeaux, Blanka/Ekwateur; TEN-0001..0004) each carry BT-720 = 97,514,000, and so do CON-0001..0004.
  - LOT-0002: BT-709 is 74,620,000 EUR, repeated the same way on TEN-0005..0008 and CON-0005..0008.

- **The store already multiplies each lot by 4.** Its lot_results show awarded 390,056,000 for LOT-0001 (4 x 97.514M) and 298,480,000 for LOT-0002 (4 x 74.62M). These do not match the notice's own BT-709 values. They are one lot's shared ceiling counted once per supplier.
- **The served figure adds those two.** 390.056M + 298.48M = 688,536,000. That does equal the notice-level BT-118 of 688,536,000. But BT-118 is just the sum of the 8 BT-720 tender values, so it carries the same error. The notice's own BT-709s give the real framework ceiling: 97.514M + 74.62M = 172,134,000 EUR.
- **New versus old.** The served 688.5M is 4.0x the real ceiling. The old head, most likely the LOT-0001 award copy of 390.056M, was 2.27x. I could not confirm the old figure from any saved file. Matching BT-118 does not save it, because that figure is the same mechanical sum of 8 contracts. Verdict: wrong (not_additive).

verify.why:
I re-read CN 24709174 and the CANs 25228005, 25228450 and 25228307. They confirm the reader's numbers and reasoning.

What the CN says: NKM 4.2 has 3 market lots, each awarded as a framework agreement ("in Form von Rahmenverträgen"). Projects are handed out later by mini-tender ("nachgelagertes Mini-Tender-Verfahren"). Demand is 10 to 50 km a year over 2027-2029. The lots carry about 70% (D), 25% (F) and 5% (I) of the total volume, each with a 30% quantity option. The CN gives no BT-27 and no procedure total. Note that BT-765 is coded "none" even though the text clearly describes a framework, which may be why a framework guard did not fire.

What the CANs say: there is one CAN per lot, and each CAN's BT-161 is just that lot's sum. BT-300 says the award goes to the five (D) or three (F, I) bidders with the most advantageous offers.
- Los D: BT-720 offers 88,533,900 / 98,371,000 / 78,696,800 / 108,208,100 / 68,859,700. BT-710 68.86M, BT-711 108.21M, BT-161 442,669,500 = their sum.
- Los F: 38,645,750 / 42,159,000 / 35,132,500, BT-161 115,937,250.
- Los I: 7,729,150 / 8,431,800 / 7,026,500, BT-161 23,187,450.

The lot keys LOT-0001/2/3 are three distinct lots (D, F, I). No lot is counted twice and no award is a x10^k slip.

Why the lot awards cannot be added: each one adds up competing offers for a single shared call-off volume.
- The three firms that bid on all lots split their offers D:F:I as 65.6/28.6/5.7 (Vanoli), 66.0/28.3/5.7 (Rhomberg) and 65.1/29.1/5.8 (Scheuchzer). That is close to the stated 70/25/5, so each offer prices the whole lot's volume.
- If each offer priced only a 1/n share, the split would be about 58/35/7. The split of the lot sums (76/20/4) also fits 70/25/5 worse.
- Mini-tender call-offs mean no supplier has a fixed share.

Result: the served 581,794,200 CHF counts Los D about 5x and Los F and I about 3x. One coverage is 111.0M (lowest offers) to 158.8M (highest), with a mean of about 134.9M, or up to about 206M with the 30% options. The old head, 23.19M (Los I's BT-161, listed as result_value with lot=null), was also far too low. But the new figure is built from non-additive pieces and is about 423-471M too high in absolute terms, against the old figure's 88-136M too low. It is not right and not merely neutral.

verify.why:
I re-read eForms CAN 23613556, the tender's only version. It states BT-161-NoticeResult = EUR 395,524,446.39. The lot figures behind that total:
- LOT-0001: one tender, TEN-0001 (Electrabel), EUR 169,946,268.83. Its BT-27 estimate and its BT-710/711 results are the same amount.

verify.why:
I re-read CAN 19080836 (TED r2.0.9 F03, framework, 21 lots), CN 18828949 and corrigendum 18855148. I could not refute the WRONG verdict, but I would class it "farther", not "slip".

(1) Stated total: the CAN's II.1.7 gives a range as the total value of the procurement (VALUE_RANGE.TYPE=PROCUREMENT_TOTAL): LOW EUR 1,000,000, HIGH EUR 2,000,000. The CN has no estimates at all, neither for the procedure nor for any lot.

(2) Lot keys: every LOT-k section's TED-LOT_NO equals k. The 10 summed awards (RES-10..RES-20) are LOT_NO 2, 5, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 17, 19 and 20, so they are distinct lots. Each lot has a single winner and a different waste stream, so the awards add up.

(3) The sum checks out: 560,653,056 EUR. The old head, by 551's rule K, was the max award copy: lot 11, 499,814,274 EUR. The sum (280x the stated EUR 2m) is farther from the 1-2m range than the old figure (250x). That meets the "farther" condition.

(4) I disagree with the slip diagnosis. Lot 11 is not uniquely mis-scaled; every figure in the CAN is inflated:
- Five other lots each exceed the stated EUR 2m high on their own: Puin 19.49m, Grond 13.98m, Gips 13.41m, Harde kunststoffen 5.82m, KGA 3.60m.
- Without lot 11 the lots still sum to 60.8m, 30x the stated maximum.
- The other lots already span 780x (24,940 to 19.5m), so 25.6x above Puin is no clean 10^k jump.
- Bulky waste (incineration, roughly EUR 100+/t) against rubble (roughly EUR 5/t) explains that ratio.
- Divided by 100, all lots look economically sensible together: bulky waste EUR 5.0m, rubble 195k, gypsum 134k, soil 140k. That points to a uniform scale error across the whole notice, not one slipped award.

Verdict: wrong. The sum does count distinct, additive lots, but the old single-lot copy was already garbage and the sum moves further from the notice's own stated total.

verify.why:
I could not refute the reader. I re-read three notices (rate-limited GETs): CN 19147770, CAN 19465124 and F20 21519724.

**What the buyer states as the total**
- CN 19147770: the procedure total is a range of GBP 400m to 440m. The lot ranges are 280-300m, 120-140m and 10-40m. The lot highs add up to 480m, but the buyer's own global high is 440m, so the buyer did not add the lots together.
- CAN 19465124, II.1.7: TED-VAL_TOTAL is 440m with VALUE.TYPE = PROCUREMENT_TOTAL.
- CAN lot awards: RES-1/2/3 award 300m, 140m and 40m. Each equals its lot's VAL_ESTIMATED_TOTAL. The lot 2 note says these are the contract notice's upper thresholds, so they are ceilings.
- CAN lot 3: its short description is "The single source supply and maintenance of goods and services within the combined scope of Lots 1 and 2". That is the same goods bought by another route, so its ceiling overlaps lots 1 and 2 and does not add to them. 440m is exactly lots 1 + 2.
- F20 21519724: its award section (one RES-1 covering LOT_NO "1, 2, 3") still states 440m. VAL_TOTAL_BEFORE is 440m. The 500m (VAL_TOTAL_AFTER) only reflects the Covid term extension, which the notice describes as "circa GBP 500 million for the full term, inclusive of extensions".

**Checks on the sum itself**
- **Lot keys:** LOT-1..3 line up with the published LOT_NO 1, 2, 3, so there is no key double-count.
- **Slip:** no summed award is a x10^k slip.
- **Old head:** the head version's amounts carry a tender-scope award copy of 440m (result_value with lot null, from the F20 RES-1). This copy is the largest figure. Path W's preconditions (the head is an award copy, and the sum must exceed today's figure) are consistent with the old head having served 440m, which matched the stated total exactly. I did not see the old head value directly.
- **Served value:** 480m = 300 + 140 + 40. That is 40m away from the stated 440m, and it gets there only by adding the overlapping lot 3.

**Why the 500m caveat does not save it**
- 480m is closer to the post-modification 500m (20m against 60m).
- But that 500m is a modification value, not the II.1.7 / V.2.4 total of the procurement.
- The match is a coincidence: it comes from counting lot 3, not from the extension.

Verdict: wrong. The sum is farther from the buyer's stated total than the old head, and the root cause is that lot 3 is not additive.

verify.why: I read the notices myself and agree with the reader's facts. I do not agree that the sum is wrong. Tender 5278856 has procedure_key ojs:2014-295721. That key is PIN 18002514, a Reg. 1370/2007 Art. 7(2) prior notice titled 'Vergabe von SPNV-Leistungen auf den Linien RE8, RB27 und RB33'. It says the three lines may go out in one or several procedures. Both later CNs cite this PIN: 18754944 (137548-2016, RB 27, no lots) and 18754766 (137331-2016, RE 8 as lot 1 and RB 33 as lot 2). So tender-db merged two real procedures into one Tender. The head and title come from the RB 27 CAN 19389135 (2017/S 154-320030). That CAN has no lots and gives PROCUREMENT_TOTAL 1.00 EUR, and its INFO_ADD says the II.1.7 value is not the real contract value and is withheld. The old head was therefore null: the only tender-scope amount is the 1.00 sentinel result_value, and the max election does not read lot results. CANs 19045609 (cites 2016/S 098-175985) and 19045642 (cites 2016/S 077-137331) are a duplicate pair. Each has LOT-1 = LOT_NO 1 = RE 8 at 308,000,000.00 and LOT-2 = LOT_NO 2 = RB 33 at 240,000,000.00, with a total of 548,000,000.00. The TED LOT-k keys match the published LOT_NOs. Path W took one award per lot, so the duplicate CANs were not counted twice. It skipped RB 27's 1.00 sentinel on the shared LOT-1 key. Neither award looks like a slip: about 2.0m and 1.7m train-km a year over about 7 years fits 300m and 240m. The served 548m is the sum of the Tender's own two listed lots (/v1/lots shows exactly RE 8 and RB 33). It equals the stated total of the notices those lots come from, and it is the procedure figure this Tender served at versions 11-12, before the RB 27 sentinel replaced it. No rubric reason for 'wrong' applies. Nothing is counted twice, nothing slipped, the parts add up, and the sum is not farther from any real stated total, since the 1.00 is a declared placeholder. The fault is the merge that happened before path W: one LOT-1 key holds both RE 8 and RB 27, and the title is RB 27. Read as the PIN's three-line program, 548m is the disclosed part (RB 27 is withheld) and is better than null. Read as RB 27, it is another procedure's money, and null was more honest. Because the result depends on which reading you take, it is defensible but not clearly better than null: neutral. The fix belongs in the merge, not in path W's guards. Notice dumps are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-tender-db/3050fd14-5ca6-5dd7-8b63-f827e13fd8ce/scratchpad/n5278856/.

I could not refute the WRONG / not_additive call. I re-read the only notice, eForms result 23808005 (subtype 29, Paris Habitat ravalement framework, 4 lots, published 2024-03-01).

(1) The notice states no procedure total: there is no BT-161, BT-27, BT-709 or contract-level value. The only figures are the BT-24 texts and BT-720 per tender.

(2) Lots 1 to 3 are single-supplier order frameworks, distinct lots by region. BT-24 gives their maxima as 14M, 10M and 12M EUR (3.5M, 2.5M and 3M a year over 4 years). Their BT-720 figures equal those maxima exactly, which shows that BT-720 in this notice holds the framework maximum, not a bid price. The stored LOT-0004 award and the CON-0004 value of 400M are the store's own sum of the five copies; the notice itself prints no 400M anywhere. In a French multi-holder framework the maximum belongs to the framework as a whole, and the holders compete for each follow-on contract. So 80M is one shared ceiling (20M a year over 4 years, the same pattern as lots 1 to 3), not five ceilings that add up.

(3) There is no x10^k slip and no lot keyed twice: LOT-0001 to LOT-0004 match BT-22 internal ids 1 to 4.

They are still separate lots in separate districts with separate notices, so this is not a double-keyed lot. Nothing is slipped. A guard should refuse a lot whose award is the sum of its winners' bids, or use one bid per lot instead.

I re-read the tender detail and the notices myself, and the WRONG / not_additive call holds. Sources: tender 36624, the award notice 25686056 (00252589-2026, subtype 29) and the latest contract notice 25506032.

(1) Stated total. The award notice carries BT-118-NoticeResult = EUR 214,000,000. That is exactly the sum of the three lots' BT-709 framework maxima: 140M + 14M + 60M. The SDK's own rule requires BT-118 to equal the sum of BT-709. The detail never shows BT-118 (it is unmapped, issue 506), and every BT-27 estimate is a 0 sentinel, so path W's T' let the sum through.

(2) What each lot's award is. LOT-0001, -0002 and -0003 are three distinct, correctly keyed lots (eForms, one notice, no TED re-keying). But each lot's 'award' is not one award. The notice puts no amount on the settled contract. Ingest builds each lot's figure by adding up the BT-720 offers of every winner of the multi-supplier framework ('accord-cadre à marchés subséquents', fa-w-rc, selec-w):
- LOT-0001: 7 offers of 22.70M to 25.56M, total 164,236,185, against its BT-709 of 140M.
- LOT-0002: 6 offers of 3.22M to 4.21M, total 21,715,296, against 14M.
- LOT-0003: 5 offers of 11.37M to 12.27M, total 59,008,549, against 60M.

Divided by each lot's BT-24 estimated volume, every single offer prices the WHOLE lot:
- LOT-0001: about 98.6 EUR/MWh over 239,311 MWh.
- LOT-0002: about 98 EUR/MWh over 36,998 MWh.
- LOT-0003: about 53 EUR/MWh over 221,546 MWh.

So the offers in a lot are rival prices for the same volume, not shares of it. Adding them is not additive, and two lots' summed figures break their own caps.

(3) No x10^k slip anywhere.

(4) Old head. It was almost certainly the LOT-0001 award copy, EUR 164.24M (the largest copy; G0 needed the sum to be above it). The best argument for refuting: the served EUR 244.96M is 14.5% above 214M (30.96M off), while 164.24M was 23.3% below (49.76M off). So the sum is numerically closer, and this is not a 'farther' case. That closeness is a coincidence: LOT-0002 overshoots its cap by 55%, LOT-0001 by 17%, and LOT-0003 sits just under. The served figure is in effect 18 parallel supplier offers added together across three framework lots. That is exactly the rubric's not-additive shape (several suppliers' values on one framework lot), and it is no less wrong because the old single-lot copy was also an inflated aggregate. The correct served total is the stated BT-118 of EUR 214M.

The contract notice 22926733 (2023-01) gives per-lot VAL_OBJECT of 250M, 400M, 100M and 50M DKK, and VAL_ESTIMATED_TOTAL of 800M DKK, which is exactly those four added up. Each lot has its own CAN, and the four lots are different things: LOT-0001 desktops, LOT-0002 screens, LOT-0003 ultraportables, LOT-0004 printers. All are eForms keys and match BT-137. So no lot is counted twice across lots, and no award is a slip.

In each CAN the buyer's BT-161 is the exact sum of the winning offers (BT-720):
- 25207267, LOT-0001: 19,788,633.16 + 17,903,226 + 19,400,544 = 57,092,403.16. BT-759 says 3 tenders were received, all 3 won, and BT-710/711 are 17.90M / 19.79M.
- 25207223, LOT-0002: 5,762,265 + 5,429,109 = 11,191,374.
- 25207416, LOT-0003: 36,470,350 + 36,604,966 = 73,075,316.
- 25209362, LOT-0004: 6,003,722.44 + 5,806,761.70 = 11,810,484.14.

The award justification (BT-300) for lots 2-4 reads 'Les offres font partie des deux offres les plus avantageuses par lot', meaning the buyer deliberately named the top two of three bidders per lot. The competing offers for a lot are near-identical: 36.47M vs 36.60M for LOT-0003, and 17.9-19.8M for LOT-0001. That pattern means each bidder priced the same lot basket. Members buy from whichever winner they choose, so the parallel offers do not add up.

Path W's step of adding across the four distinct lots is sound. But the figure it adds for each lot is already 2-3 parallel offers summed together. The served total of 153,169,577.30 CHF therefore counts each lot's basket about 2.3 times. One offer per lot gives 65,609,446.70 (lowest winners) or 68,159,586.60 (highest winners).

The old head, 11,810,484.14, was lot 4's BT-161 alone. It was also bad: one lot out of four, and itself a two-offer sum. In ratio terms the new figure is closer to about 67M (2.3x over versus 5.7x under). In absolute terms it is farther (about 86M over versus about 55M under). Either way the served sum is built from amounts that do not add, so it falls under 'wrong / not_additive', not right or neutral.

The root cause is the per-lot award input: BT-161 on a single-lot CAN with several winners. A guard for this case would refuse a lot whose award equals the sum of 2+ winning offers in one lot. Alternatively it could use one offer per lot, such as the highest winning offer (BT-711).

The seven lots really are distinct: seven language-pair sections, LOT-0001 to LOT-0007, each with its own notice. No notice states a procedure total, and the CN gives no estimate. - Temnewo quotes 1,165,318 in lots 4, 5 and 6.
- Hieronymus quotes 1,062,839.20 in lots 4, 5 and 6.
- lawtank quotes 927,498 in lots 4 and 5.
- Swisstrade quotes 495,098 in lots 5 and 6.
- Two lot-1 bidders both quote exactly 4,842,880.

The served 114,674,425.80 CHF is therefore 58 parallel prices added together. Built per lot, a defensible total is about 3.70M using each lot's lowest offer, 8.93M using the average and 11.70M using the highest. items.old_figure: EUR 2,800,000.00, the F20 21388010 RES-1 award copy (detail amounts: result_value lot=null 280,000,000 cents)
items.stated_total: EUR 403,084.00: the F03 award notice 20499603 (2019/S 126-308967) gives procedure TED-VAL_TOTAL / TED-VALUE 40,308,400 cents with VALUE.TYPE=PROCUREMENT_TOTAL
items.why: The served sum is 294,571,200 = 280,000,000 (LOT-1, from the F20 modification notice 21388010) + 7,999,200 (LOT-2) + 6,572,000 (LOT-4). The two smaller figures come from F03 20499603. F03 20499603 states a procurement total of EUR 403,084 (40,308,400 cents). It lists LOT_NO 1 to 5 in order: lot 1 Decazeville (CRP, contract 2019_0850) at EUR 79,992; lot 2 La Tenazere (Instep) at EUR 79,992; lot 4 Souillac (CC Quercy Bouriane) at EUR 65,720; lots 3 and 5 unsuccessful. The F20 notice 21388010 (2020/S 232-572983) has a single lot section keyed LOT-1, but its published LOT_NO is 27: contract 2019_0229, concluded 2019-02-22, CC Quercy Rouergue et Gorges de l'Aveyron, Midi Quercy territory. That is a different lot. The section-order key therefore replaced lot 1's real award (EUR 79,992) with lot 27's figure. Lot 27's EUR 2.8M also does not look like that contract's own value. The notice gives EUR 2.8M as RES-1 VAL_TOTAL and as VAL_TOTAL_BEFORE/AFTER, but its DESCRIPTION_PROCUREMENT.VAL_TOTAL is only EUR 19,998 (1,999,800 cents). EUR 2.8M is about 35x the sibling lot awards and 7x the stated procedure total, so it reads like a programme or framework ceiling. Against the stated EUR 403,084, the old EUR 2.8M was off by about EUR 2.40M and the new EUR 2,945,712 is off by about EUR 2.54M, so the sum is farther away. It also drops lot 1 and adds a foreign lot 27. A better figure would be F03's EUR 403,084, or the three F03 awards, which total EUR 225,704.

items.stated_total: None. The F06 award notice 18841982 has no procedure-level total. The contract notice 18605637 gives estimates only in free text: lot 1 EUR 107,000 HT/yr, lot 2 EUR 273,000 HT/yr
items.why: The served sum is 30,207,220 = 9,604,488 + 20,602,732. Both figures come from the F06 award notice 18841982 (2016/S 130-233077), which states no procedure total. Its RES-1 is LOT_NO 1 'Pieces pour le reseau': Point P, contract 16M361, 4 tenders, VAL_TOTAL EUR 96,044.88. Its RES-2 is LOT_NO 2 'Pieces pour les branchements': SOVAL Toulouse, contract 16M362, 5 tenders, VAL_TOTAL EUR 206,027.32. The section keys LOT-1 and LOT-2 match the published LOT_NO 1 and 2, and the contract notice 18605637 (2015/S 233-424190) also lists LOT_NUMBER 1 and 2. So these are two distinct lots, each with one supplier and one award. INFO_ADD says the amounts are the winning bidders' DQE figures (priced quantity estimates) on purchase-order contracts with no minimum or maximum. Each award is that lot's own priced estimate rather than a shared ceiling, so the two add up. Neither figure is a slip: they are 0.90x and 0.75x of the contract notice's annual estimates (EUR 107,000 and EUR 273,000), whose combined EUR 380,000/yr is close to the sum of EUR 302,072.20. With no stated total, the sum of two distinct real awards beats serving one lot's copy.

verify.why:
I re-read both notices and could not refute the reader. Every point checks out.

The served value is 294,571,200 cents (EUR 2,945,712), summed from three lots:
- LOT-1: 280,000,000, from F20 notice 21388010, which is the newest notice.
- LOT-2: 7,999,200, from F03 notice 20499603.
- LOT-4: 6,572,000, from F03 notice 20499603.

The stated total: F03 20499603 (2019/S 126-308967) gives a procedure-level TED-VAL_TOTAL / VALUE.TYPE=PROCUREMENT_TOTAL of 40,308,400 cents (EUR 403,084). That notice has FRAMEWORK=1 and LOT_NO 1 to 5 in document order. Its awards:
- Lot 1, Decazeville: CRP, contract 2019_0850, EUR 79,992.
- Lot 2, La Tenazere: Instep, contract 2019_0851, EUR 79,992.
- Lot 4, Souillac: CC Quercy Bouriane, contract 2019_0852, EUR 65,720.
- Lots 3 and 5: PROCUREMENT_UNSUCCESSFUL.

The lot-key collision: F20 21388010 (2020/S 232-572983) has a single lot section, keyed LOT-1 by section order. Its published LOT_NO is 27, in both the Lot and the RES-1 sections. That result is contract 2019_0229, concluded 2019-02-22, four months before the F03 contracts. The winner is CC Quercy Rouergue et Gorges de l'Aveyron, for the Midi Quercy territory (NUTS FRJ28). This is a different lot from F03 lot 1, so its figure replaced lot 1's real EUR 79,992 award.

The EUR 2.8M is not that contract's own value. It appears as RES-1 VAL_TOTAL and as VAL_TOTAL_BEFORE/AFTER. DESCRIPTION_PROCUREMENT.VAL_TOTAL is only EUR 19,998, and the modification only corrects HT unit prices (EUR 2,873.16 and 3,123.16 a year per seat). EUR 2.8M is about 35x the sibling awards and about 7x the stated procedure total, so it reads as a programme or ceiling value.

The old head served 280,000,000. That is the procedure-level result_value amount, a copy of the F20 award. Measured against EUR 403,084:
- Old figure: off by EUR 2,396,916.
- New sum: off by EUR 2,542,628.

So the sum is farther from the stated total. It also adds a foreign lot 27 and drops real lot 1. A better figure would be F03's EUR 403,084 total, or EUR 225,704 if only the three real awards are summed.
